title: What Happens When You Grab a Bass With Dry Hands?
hook: You've been holding bass wrong, and it starts with dry hands.
script: You've been holding bass wrong, and it starts with dry hands. Dry hands strip the fish's protective slime, which raises its risk of infection and disease. Fingers under the gill cover or in the eye sockets? Never. A hot engine cover or carpeted deck? Also no. Even wet cloth gloves may rub off extra slime and spread disease from fish to fish. So wet your bare hands, grip the lower jaw without bending it back, and keep it out no longer than you can hold your breath.

claims.text: Dry hands remove a fish's protective slime, raising the risk of infection and disease.
Never hold a fish with fingers under the gill cover or in the eye sockets.
Avoid hot surfaces like engine covers.
Wet cloth gloves may remove extra slime and spread disease between fish.
Hands should be bare or in smooth rubber gloves.
Hold black bass by the lower jaw without hyper-extending it.
Keep a fish out of water no longer than you can hold your breath.
